entryPoint: Topic::isActive() in include/class.topic.php (lines 194-196); Topic::isEnabled() (lines 190-192) is a pure one-line delegate — `return $this->isActive();` — and is treated as the same facade surface per ticket instructions.
coreLogic: Topic::isActive() reads the already-hydrated instance property $this->flags (an int bitmask column on ost_help_topic, loaded by the VerySimpleModel ORM via Topic::lookup()) and returns !!($this->flags & Topic::FLAG_ACTIVE), where FLAG_ACTIVE = 0x0002 (defined at include/class.topic.php:70, alongside FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS = 0x0001 and FLAG_ARCHIVED = 0x0004). The double-negation (!!) coerces the raw bitwise-AND result (an int, 0 or 2) into a strict PHP bool. Topic::isEnabled() has zero independent logic — it only forwards to isActive() and performs no additional checks.
consumers: include/class.topic.php:191 — Topic::isEnabled() delegates directly to isActive(); many outside callers use isEnabled() interchangeably with isActive() (e.g. dynamic form field enable/disable templates use the generic isEnabled() name, though those specific templates operate on DynamicFormField, not Topic — confirmed Topic-typed isEnabled() call sites are limited to this internal delegation).

include/staff/filter.inc.php:253 — staff Filter edit page; after Topic::lookup($config['topic_id']), if !$topic->isActive() sets a non-fatal $_warn message shown next to the 'Set Help Topic' filter action row.

scp/filters.php:150 — staff Filters list controller; after Topic::lookup($config['topic_id']) from a filter's stored action config, if !$topic->isActive() sets $warn, rendered as a banner warning that the filter targets an inactive help topic.

include/class.ticket.php:3686 (Ticket::update()) — after Topic::lookup($vars['topicId']), if $topic exists and !$topic->isActive() sets $errors['topicId'], blocking the ticket update as a validation failure.

include/class.ticket.php:4213-4214 (Ticket::create() validation) — gates entry into the topic-specific dynamic-form validation branch: only iterates $topic_forms and validates topic-scoped fields when Topic::lookup(...) succeeds AND $topic->isActive() is true; if the topic is not active, $vars['topicId'] is reset to 0 instead.

include/class.ticket.php:4268-4269 (Ticket::create(), email-derived ticket path) — when no topic was already resolved, calls $T = $email->getTopic() then checks ($T->isActive()); only assigns $topic = $T (adopting the email's associated help topic as the ticket's topic) if the email's topic is active.

include/class.filter.php:639-646 (Filter::save()/action validation) — for a 'topic' type filter action, after Topic::lookup($config['topic_id']), if (!$topic || !$topic->isActive()) sets a fatal $errors['err'], blocking the filter action from being saved with an inactive topic.

include/class.filter_action.php:534-538 (FA_AssignTopic::apply(), executed when a ticket filter runs against an incoming ticket) — after Topic::lookup($config['topic_id']), only sets $ticket['topicId'] = $config['topic_id'] (mutating the in-progress ticket vars array by reference) when $topic->isActive() is true; otherwise the assignment is silently skipped and the topic is left unset.

include/class.filter_action.php:558-562 (FA_AssignTopic::getConfigurationOptions(), staff UI) — after Topic::lookup($topic_id['topic_id']) for the currently-configured value, if $topic && !$topic->isActive() it force-adds that inactive topic back into the $choices dropdown (keyed by topic id/name) so the previously-selected inactive topic still appears as an option in the filter-action editor.

include/class.config.php:1425-1428 (OsticketConfig::updateTicketsSettings()) — after Topic::lookup($vars['default_help_topic']), if $T exists and !$T->isActive() sets $errors['default_help_topic'], blocking the System Settings > Tickets save when the chosen default help topic is inactive.
inputShape: None — isActive() and isEnabled() are zero-argument instance methods. The only 'input' is the object's own already-loaded $flags int property (populated earlier by the ORM when the Topic row was fetched via Topic::lookup() or Topic::objects()).
outputShape: bool — true when the FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0002) bit is set in $this->flags, false otherwise. Not the raw bitmask int; the !! cast guarantees a strict boolean. No mutation of the Topic object and no new object is returned.
sideEffects: None inside isActive()/isEnabled() themselves — both are pure reads of an in-memory instance property with no DB queries, no writes, no global state access ($cfg or otherwise), no caching, and no file I/O.

Indirect/contextual only: nearly every call site first performs a DB read via Topic::lookup($id) (or Ticket::getTopic() / Email::getTopic(), which themselves call Topic::lookup()) to hydrate the Topic object before isActive() is invoked; that lookup/hydration is the caller's responsibility, not part of isActive()'s own behavior, and must remain unaffected by this extraction.

Several consumers use the boolean result to drive their own side effects downstream of the check (not side effects of isActive() itself): e.g. FA_AssignTopic::apply() mutates $ticket['topicId'] by reference only when isActive() returns true; Ticket::create()'s email path sets $topic = $T only when active; several validation call sites populate an $errors array element when isActive() returns false.
constraints: Must preserve the exact bit test: (flags & 0x0002) != 0, using FLAG_ACTIVE only — must not conflate with FLAG_ARCHIVED (0x0004) or FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS (0x0001); a topic can have other bits set (e.g. FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS) while still being active, and the check must remain a bitwise AND against FLAG_ACTIVE alone, not an equality comparison against the whole flags value.

Return type must remain strict bool (matching the current !! coercion), not the raw masked int, since callers use it directly in boolean contexts (! negation, ternaries, && chains) and as array/config gates.
Zero-argument, no-side-effect signature must be preserved exactly — extraction must not require callers to pass flags explicitly or change how/when the Topic object is hydrated.

Topic::isEnabled() must continue to return the identical value as Topic::isActive() for every Topic (no divergent logic introduced) since some code paths conceptually treat 'enabled' and 'active' as synonyms for Topic.

The extracted service must not call back into Topic::isActive() or Topic::isEnabled() (would reintroduce the coupling the extraction is meant to remove) — it must implement the bitmask check independently against a passed-in flags value, with the facade methods on Topic delegating out to it.

Topic::getHelpTopics() (include/class.topic.php:338) independently re-implements the same bitmask check ($flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE) for building topic lists, bypassing isActive() entirely — this is out of scope for extraction, but confirms FLAG_ACTIVE's value/semantics must not change as a side effect of this work.
No timezone, locale, or precedence/fallback logic is involved; this is a stateless boolean derivation with no ordering or guard dependencies beyond the flags bit itself.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field: "flags" (int) — the raw help-topic flags bitmask to test against FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0002), e.g. 0 (disabled, no flags), 2 (active only), 4 (archived only, inactive), 6 (active + archived simultaneously — must still resolve true since FLAG_ACTIVE bit is set), 1 or 3 (custom-numbers flag alone / combined with active) to cover the 'active-plus-other-flags' case. The harness should construct/hydrate a Topic instance with the given flags value and invoke isActive() (and optionally isEnabled(), which must match) to capture the boolean output for parity comparison.
